A patient presents with 12-day history of progressive right knee pain and swelling, without systemic symptoms (afebrile, no chills or malaise). Physical exam details (erythema, warmth, stiffness, instability) are incomplete/undocumented.

- Right knee ultrasound with Doppler — *findings not reported*  
- Arthrocentesis performed:

The synovial fluid profile meets criteria for *septic arthritis* (WBC >25,000/mm³, >75% PMNs) — though Gram stain negativity lowers but does not exclude bacterial infection. Alternatively, *crystal-induced arthritis* (e.g., gout or CPPD) remains possible, particularly if crystals are identified on polarized microscopy.

Among all possibilities consistent with the data, septic arthritis has the strongest *direct laboratory support*: the synovial WBC and differential are diagnostic-level findings per widely accepted criteria (e.g., ACR, IDSA), whereas crystal disease remains *unconfirmed and less temporally congruent*. Pending culture positivity would confirm it, but pre-test probability — grounded in objective synovial fluid metrics — favors septic arthritis.

- Synovial fluid WBC = 26,000/mm³ (>25,000/mm³ threshold for septic arthritis)  
- Neutrophil percentage = 75% (meets ≥75% PMN criterion for septic arthritis)  
- Synovial fluid appearance is cloudy (consistent with inflammatory/infectious effusion)  
- Gram stain is negative (does not exclude infection; expected false-negative rate acknowledged)  
- Duration is 12 days — longer than typical self-limited gout flare, raising concern for untreated infection  

[GAPS]  
- Synovial fluid aerobic (and anaerobic/fungal) culture results are pending  
- Crystal analysis (polarized microscopy) result is not reported  
- No documented risk factors for septic arthritis (e.g., skin infection, recent surgery, immunosuppression, IV drug use)  
- No documented risk factors for crystal arthritis (e.g., hyperuricemia, chronic kidney disease, age >60, prior gout)  
- No imaging findings (e.g., X-ray for chondrocalcinosis, US for double-contour sign or calcifications)  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Septic arthritis
